# 0x226 — `mode_tcs`

DLC 7 · 100 Hz · status: **confirmed**

Riding mode and traction-control setting, sent continuously. The value changes only when the rider changes a setting.

## Layout

Bytes are numbered from 0. Multi-byte values are big-endian unless a row says otherwise. Bit 7 is the most significant bit of a byte.

| Byte | Content |
|---|---|
| B0 | `ride_mode`, `tcs_pattern` |
| B1 | — |
| B2 | — |
| B3 | `tcs_level` |
| B4 | — |
| B5 | `tcs_level_b5`, `setting_2bit` |
| B6 | — |

## Signals

| Signal | Where | Type | Value | Unit | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ride_mode` | B0 bits 7..6 | 2-bit field | enum |  | confirmed (medium) |
| `tcs_pattern` | B0 bits 3..0 | 4-bit field | enum |  | confirmed (high) |
| `tcs_level` | B3 | uint8 | enum |  | confirmed (high) |
| `tcs_level_b5` | B5 bits 3..2 | 2-bit field | raw |  | confirmed (high) |
| `setting_2bit` | B5 bits 1..0 | 2-bit field | raw |  | hypothesis (medium) |

### `ride_mode`

Riding mode (see 0x209 `ride_mode`).

| Raw | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | D-MODE 1 |
| 1 | D-MODE 2 |
| 2 | D-MODE 3 |
| 3 | D-MODE 4 |

**Confirmed by:** The dash on video with spoken markers.

**How we know:** The rider stepped through the four modes with the dash in the frame; this field followed each step.

**Example:** `0x226  0F 01 00 03 00 2D 00` → 0

### `tcs_pattern`

The 2-bit traction-control level written twice: 0x5, 0xA or 0xF.

| Raw | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | probably TCS OFF (not confirmed) |
| 5 | TCS 1 |
| 10 | TCS 2 |
| 15 | TCS M |

**Confirmed by:** Copy of `tcs_level` in the same frame; nothing outside the bus.

**How we know:** Always equal to B3 written twice, in every frame of every capture; one transitional value seen once at a change.

**Example:** `0x226  0F 01 00 03 00 2D 00` → 15

### `tcs_level`

Traction-control setting. Levels 1 and 2 can be switched while riding with the throttle closed; M can be entered or left only at a standstill, and the captures agree: every change into or out of M happened at 0 km/h.

| Raw | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | probably TCS OFF (not confirmed) |
| 1 | TCS 1 |
| 2 | TCS 2 |
| 3 | TCS M (manual) |

**Confirmed by:** The dash on video with spoken markers.

**How we know:** 12 changes of mode and TCS level in one filmed session, each matched to the value on the dash; 13 TCS changes across all sessions.

**Example:** `0x226  0F 01 00 03 00 2D 00` → 3

### `tcs_level_b5`

Copy of `tcs_level`. B5 = 0x20 + level × 4 + `setting_2bit`, which fits every frame of a 42-minute ride.

**Confirmed by:** Copy of `tcs_level` in the same frame; nothing outside the bus.

**How we know:** The formula fits 253 833 of 253 833 frames of one ride and every frame of three others.

### `setting_2bit`

A two-bit rider setting that the ABS unit repeats in 0x268 B4 bits 4..3: the two are equal in every paired frame. It read 1 in every early capture and 2 in every later one, never changing within a session, and it is independent of the TCS level. Candidate: brake control mode (BC1 / BC2). Not verified.

**Example:** `0x226  0F 01 00 03 00 2D 00` → 1

> The very first frame after power-on reads `05 01 00 01 00 25 28` whatever the real settings; the real values follow within 10 ms.

> B1 is always 0x01; B2, B4 and B6 are 0x00 in normal frames.
